play_failure_diagnosis:
Nobody has seen the Play Console rejection text: it isn't in the repo or in the gh run history. This ranking is built from code and dates, and the Console text outranks all of it.

PAST failures, VERIFIED from the repo:
(1) The May 14 build was rejected for Broken Functionality. The Map tab crashed because the packaged manifest had no com.google.android.geo.API_KEY (commit 4870127d; android/app/build.gradle.kts:24-28). The fix is on main at AndroidManifest.xml:156-158.
(2) The May 18 resubmission was android-release run #12 at 2ad9a47b, the last release run (gh run list). Its in-app Delete Account POSTed an empty body (git show 2ad9a47b:.../ProfileViewModel.kt:192). The server's SEC-025 two-step flow had been rejecting that with a 400 since 0b701939 (2026-03-28). The legacy no-body branch at supabase/functions/delete-user-account/index.ts:430-447 only arrived on 2026-08-11. A reviewer checking account deletion would have seen it fail, so this is the most likely cause of the latest failure (SUSPECTED, confidence medium-high).
(3) Second candidate: a User Data / Data safety mismatch. src/pages/PrivacyPolicy.tsx:98 says 'not precise GPS', but the May binary already declared ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION (2ad9a47b AndroidManifest.xml:7).
(4) Third: 'Continue with Google' does nothing visible. AuthScreen.kt:619-639 only logs the error, and the historical google-services.json has oauth_client=0 (SUSPECTED).

RULED OUT as the past cause: targetSdk 35 was compliant in May (the API 36 requirement started 2026-08-31, and main is already on 36 at build.gradle.kts:89). Ads, AD_ID and firebase-analytics all landed after the upload (aa90d236 on 2026-06-27, 2e8541756 on 2026-06-26). 16 KB alignment is fine (every PT_LOAD is 0x4000). There are no exact-alarm, foreground-service or photo/video permissions. The local app-release.aab is an unsigned May 14 build, not the run #12 artifact, so it isn't evidence of what Play received.

NEXT-UPLOAD blockers, VERIFIED in code, which is where the loop works:
- The declarations contradict the binary. docs/mobile/GOOGLE_PLAY_SUBMISSION.md:69-70 says 'no ads', but AdSlot, the interstitial and sponsored picks are mounted. The merged release manifest has AD_ID, ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID and ACCESS_ADSERVICES_ATTRIBUTION (:80-82), pulled in by firebase-analytics, and nothing first-party needs them. The privacy policy denies GPS.
- Reviewer-path no-ops: a successful sign-up is shown as an error (AuthRemoteDataSource.kt:92-100 plus the trigger conflict at 20261004000001:66-82). Google Sign-In fails silently. Subscribe returns silently when there are no ProductDetails (SubscriptionViewModel.kt:65-71), and the screen falls back to hardcoded $4.99/$12.99 (SubscriptionScreen.kt:360,380). The auth-callback branch is empty (MainActivity.kt:333-338). Remind Me is dead (EventDetailScreen.kt:712-719).
- Subscriptions policy gaps: no auto-renew/cancel disclosure, no manage link, VIP perks Android doesn't deliver (SubscriptionScreen.kt:386-391), and an upgrade path that can double-bill (no SubscriptionUpdateParams anywhere).
- The release pipeline has never shipped from current main. Signature verification can't fail (android-release.yml:339; jarsigner exits 0 on an unsigned jar). The versionCode floor is the committed 6, not Play's maximum. A placeholder Google client ID only produces a warning.
rationale:
I'm chairing, and I accepted the corrections every reviewer agreed on. Past causes and next-upload blockers are kept apart. Adding pipefail alone is not a fix for the signature check. Assetlinks waits until the deep-link parser resolves slugs. The client profile insert stays and treats 23505 as success, because the trigger migration isn't verified live. The loop makes no MIN_SUPPORTED_APP_VERSION change, doesn't touch the delete-user-account legacy branch, and adds no new rejections in validate-android-receipt (the May 1.0.0 binary still depends on them). No annual SKUs until the server allowlist ships. No dependency bumps before the first bundleRelease on AGP 9.3.2.

Order follows the rules. Stories 1-17 clear Play-review blockers: the manifest and consent mismatch first, then the reviewer path in the order a reviewer taps, then paywall policy, then deletion, then the web compliance pages and the submission packet. Stories 18-20 harden the release pipeline (build health). Stories 21-23 are reliability. Stories 24-25 are the parity work the user asked for: the brand palette and launch polish, then the Home IA rebuild, split so each fits one sitting. Every story is client-only Android code, CI YAML, or an additive web route or text. Nothing changes an edge function, an RPC or a schema.

Branch: fix/android-overhaul already exists and sits exactly at origin/develop (0/0), which fits CLAUDE.md's fix/* off develop rule. Work returns to develop by PR, and the Play build comes from a release/x.y.z cut, never develop -> main.

Verification is memory-safe. Each iteration runs one Gradle invocation with --no-daemon, a single worker and an in-process Kotlin compiler, after gradlew --stop. android-ci.yml runs on the branch through workflow_dispatch, because the pull_request trigger was removed in PR #447. Things the loop can't decide (Console values, fingerprints, GCP, legal wording, prod accounts, the backend target) are human tasks. Stories that depend on them are written so they work without those values and read them from repo variables later.

stories.title: Remove AD_ID/AdServices permissions and default Firebase Analytics off until consent
stories.description: firebase-analytics merges com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID, ACCESS_ADSERVICES_ATTRIBUTION and ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID into the release manifest (merged manifest :80-82). Nothing first-party needs them, because ads are served by CampaignAdService. Strip them, stop analytics from collecting before consent is applied, and make sure CI catches it if they come back.
acceptance_criteria: The source manifest declares xmlns:tools and has <uses-permission tools:node="remove"> entries for com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID, android.permission.ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID and android.permission.ACCESS_ADSERVICES_ATTRIBUTION
The manifest has <meta-data> firebase_analytics_collection_enabled=false and google_analytics_adid_collection_enabled=false inside <application>
DesMoinesInsiderApp injects AnalyticsService (or calls an apply-consent method on it) in onCreate, so stored consent is applied at process start, not on first lazy construction
AnalyticsService only calls setAnalyticsCollectionEnabled(true) when consent is granted. The 'essential events bypass' comment is corrected, since disabled collection drops those events

A new JVM test, ManifestPermissionAllowlistTest, reads src/main/AndroidManifest.xml (same file-reading pattern as DeepLinkManifestParityTest) and fails if any of the three removals or two meta-data entries is missing. It also fails if a dangerous permission outside the allowlist (INTERNET, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION, POST_NOTIFICATIONS, VIBRATE, RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED, USE_BIOMETRIC and the others the source already declares) is added

android-ci.yml gets a step after 'assembleRelease' that greps android/app/build/intermediates/merged_manifest/release/processReleaseMainManifest/AndroidManifest.xml and exits 1 if AD_ID or ACCESS_ADSERVICES appears
stories.verification: Run the baseline with --tests '*ManifestPermissionAllowlistTest*' --tests '*AnalyticsServiceTest*'. Then run, single-worker and no-daemon: cd android && ./gradlew --no-daemon --max-workers=1 -Pkotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process :app:processReleaseMainManifest && ! grep -E 'permission.AD_ID|ACCESS_ADSERVICES' app/build/intermediates/merged_manifest/release/processReleaseMainManifest/AndroidManifest.xml. Then dispatch android-ci.yml on fix/android-overhaul and confirm the new merged-manifest step is green.

stories.title: Paywall: no hardcoded prices, unavailable state, auto-renew disclosure, manage link, honest VIP list
stories.description: SubscriptionViewModel.kt:65-71 returns silently when ProductDetails is null. SubscriptionScreen.kt:360,380 fall back to $4.99/$12.99. The VIP rows at :386-391 and AppEnums.kt:230-233 advertise SMS alerts, reservation help, concierge and perks that Android doesn't implement. acceptance_criteria: No price string literal (regex \$[0-9]+\.[0-9]{2}) remains in SubscriptionScreen.kt or SubscriptionViewModel.kt

When ProductDetails for a tier is null, that tier's card shows 'Subscriptions unavailable right now' and the Subscribe button is disabled. A load-in-progress state shows a progress indicator, not a price

stories.title: Billing: tier change uses SubscriptionUpdateParams, purchase launch checks connection and result
stories.description: BillingService.kt:230-262 never sets SubscriptionUpdateParams, so an Insider choosing VIP buys a second concurrent subscription. launchPurchaseFlow doesn't call ensureConnected and ignores the BillingResult that launchBillingFlow returns, which leaves the spinner up until the watchdog fires. Entitlement stays decided by validate-android-receipt, and no server change is made.
acceptance_criteria: A pure planner decides the purchase mode from (currentTier, currentPurchaseToken, targetTier): New, Upgrade(oldToken, ReplacementMode.CHARGE_PRORATED_PRICE), Downgrade(oldToken, ReplacementMode.DEFERRED), or NoOp when the tiers are equal
launchPurchaseFlow attaches setSubscriptionUpdateParams with the old purchase token for Upgrade and Downgrade
launchPurchaseFlow awaits ensureConnected() and, if it fails, surfaces an error and clears the purchasing state
A non-OK BillingResult from launchBillingFlow clears the purchasing state immediately and maps to a user-visible error
The offer is chosen by base-plan id when Config names one, otherwise the first offer, and the existing behaviour stays the default
Unit tests cover the planner for all four cases
stories.verification: Run the baseline with --tests '*BillingFlowParamsBuilderTest*' --tests '*ValidationOutcomeTest*'. Then: grep -n 'setSubscriptionUpdateParams' android/app/src/main/java/com/desmoines/aipulse/data/remote/BillingService.kt must return a match.

stories.title: Release workflow: signature verification that can fail
stories.description: android-release.yml:339 pipes jarsigner -verify into tail with no pipefail, and jarsigner -verify exits 0 on an unsigned AAB anyway (verified on the local unsigned app-release.aab). :326-329 also exits 0 when build-tools are missing. Pipefail alone doesn't fix this.
acceptance_criteria: A new script, scripts/android/verify-aab-signature.sh <aab>, uses set -euo pipefail, captures the jarsigner -verify -verbose -certs output, exits 1 if it contains 'jar is unsigned' or lacks 'jar verified.', and prints the signer certificate SHA-1 via keytool -printcert -jarfile
When EXPECTED_UPLOAD_SHA1 is provided as an argument or env and is non-empty, a mismatch exits 1
The workflow step calls the script with shell: bash. A missing jarsigner or build-tools fails the step instead of exit 0
No secrets are echoed
stories.verification: bash scripts/android/verify-aab-signature.sh android/app/build/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab must exit non-zero with a message mentioning 'unsigned' (that local AAB is unsigned). Then grep -n 'verify-aab-signature.sh' .github/workflows/android-release.yml must return a match, and grep -n "| tail -20 ||" .github/workflows/android-release.yml must return nothing.

stories.title: Release workflow: explicit versionCode above a Play floor, plus lintRelease before bundleRelease
stories.description: android-release.yml:119-140 falls back to run_number and floors on the committed versionCode (6), not on what Play has accepted (possibly up to 12). The release job never runs lint. The real Play max is a human value, so it's read from a repo variable.
acceptance_criteria: The versionCode input is required. A blank value fails with ::error:: and there's no run_number fallback

The floor is max(committed versionCode in build.gradle.kts, vars.ANDROID_PLAY_MAX_VERSION_CODE when set). The input must be strictly greater than the floor. When the variable is unset, the step emits ::warning:: that the floor is only the committed value
./gradlew lintRelease runs before bundleRelease/assembleRelease in the release job
The workflow summary prints the chosen versionCode and versionName
build.gradle.kts versionCode isn't changed by this story (that needs the human Play value)

stories.title: Release workflow: assert the built AAB manifest with bundletool
stories.description: The May rejection was a manifest-content bug (geo.API_KEY missing) that a dump-and-assert would have caught. Add a post-build gate on the real artifact.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/android/assert-aab-manifest.sh <aab> <expectedVersionCode> downloads a pinned bundletool release jar (for example 1.17.2) to a temp dir if one isn't given, runs bundletool dump manifest, and exits 1 unless all of these hold: the com.google.android.geo.API_KEY meta-data has a non-empty value that isn't a placeholder; versionCode equals the expected value; targetSdkVersion >= 36; AD_ID and ACCESS_ADSERVICES_* are absent
The script also runs bundletool validate
The release workflow runs it after the build step for buildType=bundle and before uploading the artifact
No secret value is printed. The Maps key is reported only as present or absent
stories.verification: bash scripts/android/assert-aab-manifest.sh android/app/build/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab 6 must exit non-zero and name the geo.API_KEY failure (the local May AAB has none). grep -n 'assert-aab-manifest.sh' .github/workflows/android-release.yml must match.

stories.title: NetworkMonitor uses the default network; events cache keeps pagination
stories.description: NetworkMonitor.kt:73 uses registerNetworkCallback, so onLost for any one network (a wifi to LTE handoff) reports offline, and onAvailable reports online before validation. EventsRepositoryImpl.kt:29-31,44 returns hasMore=false from cache, which ends infinite scroll after the first page within the 5-minute TTL.
acceptance_criteria: NetworkMonitor uses registerDefaultNetworkCallback. Connected is derived from onCapabilitiesChanged with NET_CAPABILITY_INTERNET and NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED, and onLost of the default network sets offline

The connectivity decision is a pure function, unit-tested for a default network lost while another stays up (still connected once the new default arrives) and for available but unvalidated (not connected)
The events cache stores totalCount and hasMore with the page, or bypasses the cache for offset > 0, so a cached first page reports hasMore=true when more rows exist
fetchEvent's cache read respects the TTL
Unit tests cover the cached page-one hasMore behaviour
stories.verification: Run the baseline with --tests '*NetworkReconnectTest*' --tests '*EventsRepositoryCacheTest*' --tests '*PaginationGuardTest*'. Then grep -n 'registerDefaultNetworkCallback' android/app/src/main/java/com/desmoines/aipulse/util/NetworkMonitor.kt must match.

stories.title: suspendRunCatching: stop logging coroutine cancellation as errors in the data layer
stories.description: There are 121 runCatching sites and only 7 handle CancellationException. EventsRepositoryImpl.kt:36-45 logs cancellation through AppLogger.network.error, which DesMoinesInsiderApp.kt:49-54 forwards to crash upload. That floods log-error and can set error UI state when the user navigates away. Scope this to data/repository and data/remote so it fits one sitting.
acceptance_criteria: suspendRunCatching { } returns Result but rethrows CancellationException
Every runCatching in android/app/src/main/java/com/desmoines/aipulse/data/repository and data/remote that wraps a suspend call is replaced. Non-suspend runCatching (JSON parsing) may stay
Unit tests: a cancelled block rethrows; another exception becomes Result.failure
The ui/ layer is out of scope and left for a later story
stories.verification: Run the baseline with --tests '*SuspendRunCatchingTest*' (the full unit suite in the baseline must stay at or above the 340 floor). Then: grep -rn 'runCatching' android/app/src/main/java/com/desmoines/aipulse/data/repository | grep -v suspendRunCatching should list only non-suspend sites, each justified in the commit message.

stories.title: Deep-link parser: exact host match, web landing segments, /stay, /articles, /search; no re-apply on recreate
stories.description: DeepLinkHandler.kt:120 matches the host with contains (iOS fixed this as IOS-DD-PLATFORM-10). :136-144 turn /events/today into Event("today"). Hotels are parsed at /hotels, but web serves /stay/:slug (src/App.tsx:559-560). /articles and /search?q= aren't claimed. MainActivity.kt:111 re-applies the URI on every onCreate. Port ios/DesMoinesInsider/Services/DeepLinkHandler.swift:198-295. assetlinks.json is NOT touched in this story.
acceptance_criteria: https hosts are compared with exact equality against desmoinesinsider.com and www.desmoinesinsider.com

/events/{today,tonight,this-weekend,free,kids,suburbs,...} (the web's SEO landing routes in src/App.tsx:502-521) and /restaurants/{open-now,new,...} map to the matching tab or list destination, never to a detail id
/stay/<slug> maps to Hotel, /articles/<slug> to Article, /search?q= to Search(query). Unknown paths fall back to an in-app WebView of the URL
Detail destinations carry a slug-or-id value object (isUuid flag) for AND-OVH-022 to resolve
The manifest intent filters add pathPrefix /stay, /articles and /search, and DeepLinkManifestParityTest still passes (extend it if it covers paths)
MainActivity skips handleDeepLinkIntent when savedInstanceState != null and clears intent.data after handling

DeepLinkHandlerTest is rewritten so the old Event("touch-a-truck-2026-05-22")-as-id and Hotel("surety") assertions become slug assertions. iOS cases for landing segments, /stay, /articles, /search and an evil host (desmoinesinsider.com.evil.io) are added
stories.verification: Run the baseline with --tests '*DeepLinkManifestParityTest*'. Then dispatch android-ci.yml on fix/android-overhaul. The pixel6api34DebugAndroidTest step (which runs DeepLinkHandlerTest) must be green. grep -n 'host.contains\|contains("desmoinesinsider' android/app/src/main/java/com/desmoines/aipulse/util/DeepLinkHandler.kt must return nothing.

stories.title: Resolve web slugs to entities (events by title-date, restaurants/hotels/articles by slug column)
stories.description: EventsRemoteDataSource.kt:124, RestaurantsRemoteDataSource.kt:221-227, AttractionsRemoteDataSource.kt:146-152 and HotelsRemoteDataSource.kt:102-106 all filter eq("id"). Web URLs carry slugs. VERIFIED in scripts/db-snapshot.json: restaurants.slug, hotels.slug and articles.slug exist. events.slug and attractions.slug do not. Event slugs are '<title-slug>-<YYYY-MM-DD>' in Central Time (src/hooks/useEventBySlug.ts:15-16).
acceptance_criteria: EventSlug.parse(slug) returns (titleSlug, LocalDate) and slugify(title) matches web createEventSlugWithCentralTime for the same inputs, with test vectors copied from the web implementation
fetchEventBySlug queries events within that Central-Time day (the same visibility filters as the list query) and picks the row whose slugified title matches
Restaurants, hotels and articles resolve via eq("slug", value) when the value isn't a UUID, otherwise eq("id")
Attractions: mirror whatever the web /attractions/:slug page does (read its hook first). If it's id-only, accept a UUID and otherwise show a not-found state with an Open on web action
No new table or column is referenced. Before merging, every column used is confirmed in scripts/db-snapshot.json
Unit tests: slug parse and slugify vectors, and the UUID vs slug branch selection
stories.verification: Run the baseline with --tests '*EventSlugTest*' --tests '*EventsRemoteDataSourceTest*'. node -e checks against scripts/db-snapshot.json that every '<table>.slug' the diff queries is present in .columns. Then dispatch android-ci.yml on the branch: green.

stories.title: Brand palette: pin colors to the iOS accent (dynamic color off, orange accent)
stories.description: Theme.kt:92 sets dynamicColor = true, and the only caller, ThemeCrossfade.kt:38, never overrides it, so every Android 12+ phone swaps the brand for wallpaper colors. Color.kt:32 makes primary BrandBlue, while iOS tints everything with AccentColor #FF6B35 light / #FF7A44 dark (Assets.xcassets/AccentColor.colorset, MainTabView.swift:163). Decision: primary = orange accent, and the existing gradient stays on primary CTAs.
acceptance_criteria: dynamicColor defaults to false and no call site passes true

PrimaryLight = #FF6B35 and PrimaryDark = #FF7A44, with a comment citing ios/DesMoinesInsider/Resources/Assets.xcassets/AccentColor.colorset. onPrimary is chosen to pass 4.5:1 for labels on primary (use a dark onPrimary if white fails), and the contrast ratio is recorded in the comment
Blue moves to secondary. Tertiary and the container colors are updated consistently for light, dark and OLED schemes
BrandColorTest asserts the primary hex values and computes the WCAG contrast of onPrimary on primary as >= 4.5 for both schemes
stories.verification: Run the baseline with --tests '*BrandColorTest*'. Then grep -n 'dynamicColor: Boolean = true' android/app/src/main/java/com/desmoines/aipulse/ui/theme/Theme.kt must return nothing.

The launch theme extends Theme.SplashScreen with windowSplashScreenBackground set per light and night, then postSplashScreenTheme. MainActivity calls installSplashScreen() before super.onCreate
values-night/themes.xml sets a dark window background and windowLightStatusBar=false
ic_launcher_monochrome.xml is a single-path, single-color vector of the mark (no gradients or fills other than one color), referenced as <monochrome> in both adaptive icon XMLs
Lint passes with no new baseline entries

stories.title: Home IA part 1: Explore hub screen and Ways-to-Explore row replace the eleven CTA cards
stories.description: HomeScreen.kt:278-309 stacks eleven identical CTA cards (duplicated at :452-483) above any content, which is the layout iOS removed in IOS-IA-001 (HomeView.swift:3-12,70-75). This story moves those destinations into an Explore hub, puts one horizontal Ways-to-Explore row and the availability-gated Trip Planner card on Home, and merges the duplicated grid/list item blocks. The Right Now weather ribbon and smart-preset rails are deferred to a later parity loop.
acceptance_criteria: Home order: header, WaysToExploreRow (Ask Pulse, Swipe/Discover, Surprise Me, Explore), the Trip Planner card only when TripPlannerAvailability != Paused (from AND-OVH-011), then the existing For You, Featured, ad slots and events list. No CTA-card stack remains

ExploreHubScreen lists Weekend, Neighborhoods, Content Hubs, Dashboard, Articles, Deals, Stay (Hotels) and Best Of, each navigating to its existing route, and is registered in NavGraph and RouteRegistrationTest
The grid and list layouts share one item-builder function. The duplicated card block at :452-483 is gone
The *HomeCard.kt files left unreferenced are deleted (grep shows no references)
The global Ask Pulse FAB (MainScreen.kt:306-318, rail :236-247) is removed, since Ask Pulse is in the row
Every existing ad slot placement on Home is kept (ad tracking contract unchanged)

verification_baseline:
Run one Gradle process at a time. No parallel builds, and never two agents building at once. If android/app/google-services.json is absent, first write the placeholder the CI uses (android-ci.yml:54-82) to that gitignored path. Never overwrite a real file or android/local.properties.

Then: cd android && ./gradlew --stop && ./gradlew --no-daemon --max-workers=1 -Pkotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process -Dorg.gradle.jvmargs="-Xmx2g -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=512m" :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug, adding a story's --tests filters to testDebugUnitTest where it names them. The unit-test floor at build.gradle.kts:300 must still hold.

Before each story is marked done: gh workflow run android-ci.yml --ref fix/android-overhaul, then gh run watch on that run. It must be green: full lint, test, the pixel6api34DebugAndroidTest managed device, assembleDebug and the R8 assembleRelease. Web stories (AND-OVH-012/013) instead run npx eslint on the touched files, npm run check-e2e-lanes and npm run build.
